notes: Every page of this Qualtrics survey has the same URL; pages are identified by their question ids (fingerprint.keys), not by URL. The extension's URL-based page matching cannot tell them apart.
QID92 is a Qualtrics 'Draw' question: a canvas signature pad with no input element. It is required to leave Page 2 and is not a capturable row.
QID180 (service-area counties) is NOT required: Next on an empty Page 2 flags QID86, QID92 and QID185 only.

The form's intro (Page 1) says this is a network-interest form, not an application, and asks the submitter to have ready: W-9, group NPI, provider NPI, certification numbers, practice addresses with their TINs, state license number and expiration, specialty taxonomy codes, supervising physician NPI (mid-levels), and top 10 CPT/HCPCS codes (DME/HIT/specialty pharmacy). Expect those on the pages after the attestation.

Interstitial seen once after Page 1 → Next: 'Your session was outdated, but we have updated you to your most recent response.' Cause: the same survey open in a second tab of the same browser (shared Qualtrics session). Its OK button was not captured with a selector (seen before probe v2); avoid it by keeping one tab per survey.
Page 3's file uploads (W-9, supporting documents, CPT list) create their <input type=file> only when clicked, so they are listed under uncapturedQuestions, not rows. None is required to advance.
Next on Qualtrics posts each page to Blue KC as a partial response. Page 2's attestation was completed and signed by the user on 2026-10-14; nothing has been submitted.

Page 5's 'Response Requested' popup is built on demand; its button selectors are structural (#Page > … > button:nth-child(n)) and were read once on 2026-10-14 — unconfirmed on replay. Button 1 'Continue Without Answering' skips, button 2 'Answer the Question' returns to the page.
The practitioner data for this form travels in the uploaded 'Blue KC Provider Roster Template' spreadsheet (Page 5), not in web fields — the roster-mapper skill's job, not this capture's.

Page 6 is a 30-option mark-all-that-apply services list. The fill engine checks a box only for a truthy word (yes/true/1/x/on/checked), so no list token can drive it today: the gap is a per-option 'list contains' transform over facility.serviceTypes.
Page 6's gate was not tested: the user ticked their services before Next, so whether the services question is required is unknown.

Page 7's count drives Page 8: Qualtrics renders exactly that many 'Provider k:' boxes (#QR\~QID97\~1…k), server-side, so only Provider 1 exists in this walk (count entered by the user). The page fingerprint (QID97) is the same for any count.

Qualtrics pipes earlier answers into question text: Page 9 reads 'What is the NPI for <name typed on Page 8>?'. Captured labels on Page 9 have the piped name replaced with '[Provider 1 name]' so this file stays value-free. The probe (and the extension's own capture) read piped text verbatim — a known gap for Qualtrics forms.

Page 9's QID96 is a Qualtrics form-field question with forced response on EVERY box: Next flags all ten Provider 1 detail fields together. Fax accepts the literal 'NA'. QID186 (NPI) was not flagged on that attempt, so whether it is required is not known.

Page 9 validates Phone Number as a real US (NANP) number in the form 'XXX-XXX-XXXX': dashes required, and neither the area code nor the exchange (middle three digits) may start with 0 or 1 — a well-formatted number with an exchange like 0xx/1xx is refused. Panel phone values are stored as digits, so a token fill needs a dashed-phone transform, and placeholder numbers will not pass.

Page 10 asks for Provider 1's hospital affiliation (name, TIN, USPS-formatted address in recipient / delivery / last-line form; the formatting example is an image). The panel has no hospital-affiliation fields — a token-catalog gap for credentialing forms generally. The provider's name is piped into the question and is redacted here as '[Provider 1 name]'.
Page 11 pipes two earlier answers into one question (provider name from Page 8, hospital name from Page 10); both are redacted in the captured label.
Page 12 raised no format error on Next with the expiration date as the user typed it; Blue KC's accepted date format(s) remain unconfirmed.
Page 13 'No' (not mid-level) leads straight to Page 14 (primary specialty); the 'Yes' branch — expected to ask for the supervising physician's NPI — was not walked.

Page 14's specialty dropdown has 146 options, all captured here. The extension's Train-forms capture and the panel's write boundary both cap option lists at 50 (CONTROL_OPTIONS_CAP), so proposing this row to the panel today would be rejected (>50) or truncated by the extension — the cap is the open cross-repo fix.
Page 15 pipes the specialty chosen on Page 14 into its question; the captured label shows '[Page 14 specialty]' instead of the chosen option.

Advance timing: Page 15 → 16 took longer than 3 s. A runner must wait for the fingerprint to CHANGE (poll), not sleep a fixed delay — an unchanged fingerprint with no errors means 'still loading', not 'refused'.

Blue KC reuses option codes across questions: value 171 is 'Durable Medical Equipment' on Page 14 and 'No secondary specialty' on Page 16. Option values are only meaningful per question; match fixed answers by label when comparing questions.
Page 17a pipes the secondary specialty chosen on Page 16 into its question; redacted as '[Page 16 secondary specialty]'.

Page 16 is a branch point: a chosen secondary specialty leads to Page 17a (its taxonomy code); changing the answer to 'No secondary specialty' (confirmed by the user) leads to Page 17b (QID215, admitting privileges) instead. Both routes are recorded on Page 16. Page 17a's own Next was never taken, so where it leads is not yet known.
Page 17b's question pipes two values that resolve EMPTY ('Does  have admitting privileges at ?') — a survey-logic quirk on Blue KC's side; the captured label is verbatim, there is nothing to redact.

Admitting-privileges questions repeat per slot: QID214 (Page 11, Provider 1 + hospital piped), QID215 (Page 17b, pipes empty, optional), QID216 (Page 18, pipes empty, REQUIRED). With one provider counted, Blue KC still shows the empty slots — a survey-logic issue to raise with them; a runner cannot answer a question that names nobody.

Page 19's location count drives Page 20 like Page 7 drives Page 8: one USPS three-line address block per location (Location 1 = #QR\~QID161\~1/13/14). USPS style needs two composed values the panel lacks as single tokens: delivery line (street + suite) and last line (City ST ZIP).
Page 21 pipes Location 1's recipient line (typed on Page 20) into its question; redacted as '[Location 1 recipient line]'.
Page 22 pipes Location 1's recipient line into its question; redacted as '[Location 1 recipient line]'.

Page 23 (QID181, text only) is the FINAL page: 'Click on the "Next" button below to submit this form now. This form will not submit until you click the "Next" button.' Its button is captioned 'Next' yet SUBMITS. Probe v2 now reads page copy and reports such an advance as kind 'submit' (submitWarning: true); before that fix it was classified 'advance' and a caption-trusting runner would have submitted. The walk stopped here; nothing was submitted.

rows.label: Number of providers:
rows.formSection: How many providers are being added with this form?
rows.evidence: Claude: a per-submission count (the practitioners on the uploaded roster); no token holds it. Likely drives how many provider sections the survey shows next.

rows.label: Provider 1:
rows.formSection: Please list the names of the providers you will be adding through this form.
rows.evidence: Claude: first provider being added → the case's provider. Medium: right for a one-provider form; further providers on the same form (Provider 2…N) are not this case's provider and stay manual.
rows.revealedBy: Page 7 'Number of providers' ≥ 1 — Qualtrics renders one 'Provider k:' box (#QR\~QID97\~k) per provider counted there

rows.label: Title:
rows.formSection: Please provide the following information about [Provider 1 name], the first provider mentioned.
rows.evidence: Claude: 'Title' beside 'Degree Type' in the provider block — most likely the professional title/credentials (e.g. 'PT, DPT'); could also mean an honorific. Low until a person confirms what Blue KC expects.

rows.label: Degree Type:
rows.formSection: Please provide the following information about [Provider 1 name], the first provider mentioned.
rows.evidence: Claude: label 'Degree Type' → provider.degree.

rows.label: Gender:
rows.formSection: Please provide the following information about [Provider 1 name], the first provider mentioned.
rows.evidence: Claude: label 'Gender' in the provider block → provider.gender.

rows.label: Provider Type:
rows.formSection: Please provide the following information about [Provider 1 name], the first provider mentioned.
rows.evidence: Claude: 'Provider Type' is the discipline (PT, OT, NP…), which the state license's type carries; provider.specialty is the alternative if Blue KC wants the specialty name.

rows.label: Fax Number: (if none type "NA")
rows.formSection: Please provide the following information about [Provider 1 name], the first provider mentioned.
rows.evidence: Claude: provider fax = the practice location's fax. Medium: when the location has no fax the form wants the literal 'NA', which needs a fallback.

rows.label: Phone Number:
rows.formSection: Please provide the following information about [Provider 1 name], the first provider mentioned.
rows.evidence: Claude: for network/directory purposes the provider's phone is the practice phone (facility.phone); provider.phone is the provider's own number. Blue KC requires a valid US number as XXX-XXX-XXXX (area code and exchange may not start with 0/1), so the map needs a dashed-phone transform.

rows.label: Ever opted out of Medicare? (Y/N)
rows.formSection: Please provide the following information about [Provider 1 name], the first provider mentioned.
rows.displayLabel: Provider 1: ever opted out of Medicare (Y/N)
rows.evidence: Claude: a per-provider fact with no token; Y/N free text.

rows.formSection: Please provide the following information about [Provider 1 name], the first provider mentioned.

rows.label: Patient Gender Restrictions (M/F)

rows.label: Provider State License #:
rows.formSection: Please provide the following information about the licensure of [Provider 1 name].

rows.label: Provider License Expiration Date:
rows.formSection: Please provide the following information about the licensure of [Provider 1 name].
rows.evidence: Claude: license expiration → license.expirationDate. Medium on format: the panel stores ISO dates and Blue KC's expected date format is not yet known.

rows.label: Provider License State:
rows.formSection: Please provide the following information about the licensure of [Provider 1 name].
rows.evidence: Claude: license state → license.state.

rows.label: Is [Provider 1 name] a mid-level physician?
rows.formSection: Is [Provider 1 name] a mid-level physician?
rows.evidence: Claude: mid-level = NP/PA-type practitioners; follows from the provider's discipline (license.licenseType) but no token answers Yes/No. For a therapy org whose providers are PT/OT/SLP the answer is 'No' — medium until the org confirms. Likely a branch: Yes should add the supervising-physician NPI the intro mentions.

rows.label: What is [Provider 1 name]'s primary specialty?
rows.formSection: What is [Provider 1 name]'s primary specialty?

options.label: Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology

rows.evidence: Claude: primary specialty → provider.specialty, but Blue KC's 146-option list names professions ('Physical Therapist' = 117, 'Occupational Therapy' = 96, 'Speech/Language Pathologist' = 138) where the panel stores specialties ('Physical Therapy'), so an exact select match will miss without a value translation. Full vocabulary captured (the probe is uncapped).

rows.label: Please provide the taxonomy code for [Page 14 specialty].
rows.formSection: Please provide the taxonomy code for [Page 14 specialty].
rows.evidence: Claude: taxonomy code for the provider's specialty → provider.taxonomyCode.

rows.label: What is [Provider 1 name]'s secondary specialty?
rows.formSection: What is [Provider 1 name]'s secondary specialty?

options.label: Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology

rows.evidence: Claude: secondary specialty → provider.subSpecialty. Low: same profession-vs-specialty wording mismatch as Page 14, and an empty subSpecialty must become 'No secondary specialty' (171) — a fallback no transform provides. Note Blue KC reuses option codes: 171 is 'Durable Medical Equipment' on Page 14 but 'No secondary specialty' here, so match by label.

rows.label: Please provide the taxonomy code for  [Page 16 secondary specialty].
rows.formSection: Please provide the taxonomy code for [Page 16 secondary specialty].
rows.evidence: Claude: taxonomy code for the SECONDARY specialty; the panel holds one taxonomy code per provider (provider.taxonomyCode = primary), so a person enters this.

rows.label: Does have admitting privileges at ?
rows.formSection: Does have admitting privileges at ?
rows.displayLabel: Admitting privileges (piped names empty on this path)
rows.evidence: Claude: a second admitting-privileges question (cf. Page 11's QID214) whose piped provider and hospital names both resolve EMPTY on the 'No secondary specialty' path, so it is unclear whom it asks about — likely survey logic pointing at a source this path never filled. A person answers; worth raising with Blue KC.

rows.label: Does have admitting privileges at ?
rows.formSection: Does have admitting privileges at ?
rows.evidence: Claude: third admitting-privileges question (QID214 Page 11 → QID215 Page 17b → QID216 here), apparently one per provider/hospital slot and shown even when only one provider was counted; both piped names are empty. Unlike QID215 it is REQUIRED. A person answers; worth raising with Blue KC.

rows.label: Number of locations:
rows.formSection: How many practice locations will you be adding through this form?
rows.displayLabel: Number of practice locations being added
rows.evidence: Claude: a per-submission count of practice locations; no token holds it (a fill targets exactly one facility, so '1' per case is likely but the form may list several). Likely drives how many location sections follow, like Page 7's provider count.

rows.label: Location 1 Recipient Line:
rows.formSection: Please provide the street address of the location(s) being added to this form. The address(es) must be in the style of Postal Service standardized style, which includes all required elements and the use of Postal Service standard abbreviations. See the image below for an example.
rows.evidence: Claude: USPS recipient line = the practice location's name → facility.name (group.name if Blue KC wants the billing entity). Medium.
rows.revealedBy: Page 19 'Number of locations' ≥ 1 — one Location k block (recipient / delivery / last line) per location counted there

rows.label: Location 1 Delivery Address Line:
rows.formSection: Please provide the street address of the location(s) being added to this form. The address(es) must be in the style of Postal Service standardized style, which includes all required elements and the use of Postal Service standard abbreviations. See the image below for an example.
rows.evidence: Claude: USPS delivery line = street plus unit ('123 MAIN ST STE 200'); facility.street holds the street but the suite lives in facility.suite, so a combined line needs a transform. Medium.
rows.revealedBy: Page 19 'Number of locations' ≥ 1 — one Location k block (recipient / delivery / last line) per location counted there

rows.label: Location 1 Last Line:
rows.formSection: Please provide the street address of the location(s) being added to this form. The address(es) must be in the style of Postal Service standardized style, which includes all required elements and the use of Postal Service standard abbreviations. See the image below for an example.
rows.evidence: Claude: USPS last line = 'CITY ST ZIP' — facility.city + facility.state + facility.zip on one line; no single token composes it (facility.address includes the street).
rows.revealedBy: Page 19 'Number of locations' ≥ 1 — one Location k block (recipient / delivery / last line) per location counted there
